title: A transient Engram control failure that recovered automatically still shows as an unresolved "control degraded" alarm card
outcome: Per Greg's direction of 2026-10-11 (memory greg-decision-2026-10-11-transient-admission-self-recover, addendum): when an Engram control card reports a transient failure with an automatic retry scheduled (for example turn_begin dispatch_budget_exhausted), and a later card shows the same logical prompt admitted, the conversation view no longer leaves a prominent unresolved degraded or error card. The failure is coalesced into, or explicitly marked as, recovered, with the recovery duration and attempt count, for example "recovered automatically after 4 s (attempt 1)". The detailed diagnostics (operation, code, latencies) stay available in an expandable event-history surface. A failure that is not followed by recovery keeps its current prominent presentation, as does one whose retry was exhausted or whose outcome is truly unknown. Tests cover the recovered, still-retrying and exhausted cases. One logical prompt is preserved, with no duplicate delivery; the backend part is already covered by the exact begin replay and w-cfcf10b68c9b.
acceptance: When a degraded Engram dispatch card is followed, for the same logical prompt, by a later dispatch card that admits it, the conversation shows the degraded card as recovered: a compact status reading 'Recovered automatically after N s (attempt k)', where N is the time between the failure and the admission and k is the number of failed attempts for that prompt before it, instead of the 'Engram control degraded' alarm. The original operation, code, latency and causal-failure details stay available in an expandable section of that card.

A degraded dispatch card with no later admission of the same prompt (still retrying, exhausted, or of unknown outcome) keeps its current prominent presentation, and an admission of a different prompt never marks it recovered.
Pairing uses an explicit logical-prompt identity that the host writes on both cards, not message order. Cards written before this change, which lack that identity, render exactly as today.
The full gate passes on the exact committed tree.
